verses.46:2: Todas as nações, {plaudite}: * {jubilate} a Deus com voz de exultação.
verses.46:3: Porque o Senhor é excelso, {terribilis}: * grande Rei sobre toda a terra.
verses.46:5: Escolheu para nós a sua herança: * {speciem} de Jacó, que ele amou.
verses.46:7: {psallite1} ao nosso Deus, {psallite2}: * {psallite1b} ao nosso Rei, {psallite2b}.
verses.46:8: Porque Deus é o Rei de toda a terra: * entoai salmos {sapienter}.
verses.46:9: Deus reinará sobre as nações: * Deus {sedet} sobre o seu trono santo.
verses.46:10: Os príncipes dos povos {congregati} com o Deus de Abraão: * porque os {dii} da terra {elevati}.

decisions.why: plaudere mánibus is to clap with the hands (κροτήσατε χεῖρας; DRB 'clap your hands'). *Bater palmas* is how Portuguese says it, and the palms are the hands — the image is kept, the idiom not doubled. The cognate *aplaudi* is a bare -ir imperative that equals 'I applauded' (rule 3), and *aplaudir* now means approval rather than the clapping itself. *Batei* (-er) is not a past form (*bati*).

options.label: batei palmas com as mãos
options.note: names *mánibus* as a separate word; redundant in Portuguese.

options.label: aplaudi com as mãos
options.note: the literal tier; refused — bare -ir imperative = 'I applauded' (rule 3).

decisions.why: jubiláre / júbilus / jubilátio is one Latin family (13 lines by grep: 46:2, 46:6, 65:1, 80:2, 88:15, 94:1–2 — the Invitatory —, 97:4, 97:6, 99:2a, 150:5) and in 46:2 and 46:6 one Greek family (ἀλαλάξατε, ἐν ἀλαλαγμῷ): the shout raised to a king. The Portuguese pair that keeps the root through verb and noun is *aclamar / aclamação*; and 32:3 already has *com aclamação* for *in vociferatióne*, which is ἐν ἀλαλαγμῷ too (D15's test). The cognates fail: *jubilai* is heard in Brazil as 'retire' (or, in universities, 'be expelled'), and *júbilo* is proposed by the open gáudium row (20:7, 29:12), which names 46:6 as the collision — giving the jubil- family *aclamar* leaves *júbilo* to gáudium. *exultar* is exsultáre's, and stands in the same verse (*in voce exsultatiónis*). MS1932 *celebrai*, DRB 'shout unto', DM1962 *aclamai*. Proposed as an open row.

options.label: aclamai
options.note: Ruling; DM1962 *aclamai a Deus*; with `jubilo` *entre aclamações* the root is kept in both verses.

options.label: jubilai
options.note: the cognate; *jubilar* is 'retire / be expelled' in Brazil. Goes with *em júbilo* in `jubilo`.

decisions.why: *in* + ablative of the circumstance: God goes up amid the shout (DRB 'with jubilee'; MS1932 *entre (vozes de) júbilo*). The noun follows `jubilate`. *entre aclamações* makes the singular plural (number is grammar, D27) and says at once that the shouts are others', round him; *com aclamação* (= 32:3) could be heard as God acclaiming. The Ascension liturgy quotes this colon in another Latin, *in jubilatióne* (grep: Pasc5-4, Pasc6-0, Sancti/10-07, Benedictio mensae) — the same family, so the same Portuguese word would serve it.

options.label: com aclamação
options.note: the singular and 32:3's phrase; may be heard as God acclaiming.

options.label: em júbilo
options.note: the cognate (MS1932 *entre … júbilo*, DRB 'with jubilee'); breaks the root pair with *aclamai* and takes the gáudium row's word.

decisions.why: terríbilis (φοβερός) is 'to be feared, dreadful'. The cognate *terrível* is DRB's and MS1932's and the Latin's word, and is still said of God in Brazilian prayer; but in everyday speech it has worn down to 'very bad'. *temível* says exactly 'to be feared' and is plain. Ruled for the cognate, beside *excelso* and *grande Rei*, where 'very bad' is not a possible hearing; the blind reader is the test. The Latin's asyndeton (*excélsus, terríbilis*) is kept (DRB 'high, terrible'); MS1932 supplies *e*. terríbilis recurs (65:3, 75:8, 88:8, 95:4, 98:3, 110:9 *sanctum et terríbile nomen ejus*) — proposed as an open row.

options.label: temível
options.note: the sense without the worn edge.

decisions.why: subjícere → *sujeitar* (8:8 *Tudo sujeitastes*, 17:48 *sujeitais os povos*, row open). The dative *nobis* as an enclitic (*Sujeitou-nos os povos*) is first heard as 'he subjected us' — the opposite sense — before *os povos* corrects it; *a nós* after the object cannot be misheard (MS1932 *Submeteu os povos a nós*). The Latin perfect is kept (the Hebrew has an imperfect; rule 1).

options.label: Sujeitou-nos os povos
options.note: shorter; heard first as 'he subjected us'.

decisions.why: The subtus / sub row gives *sob*, but says a psalm that wants the living preposition may keep *debaixo de*, as 8:8 did — and 8:8 is this same collocation, subjícere … sub pédibus (*Tudo sujeitastes debaixo dos seus pés*). The echo is kept. MS1932 *debaixo dos nossos pés*.

options.label: sob os
options.note: the row's default (17:10 *sob os seus pés*).

decisions.why: spécies here is καλλονή, 'beauty' (DRB 'the beauty of Jacob'), in apposition to *hereditátem*. decor is already *esplendor* (20:6, 25:8, 29:8), so that word is taken. *beleza* is the plain word; *formosura* is kept free for 44:5a, where *spécie tua et pulchritúdine tua* sets spécies (ὡραιότης) beside pulchritúdo (κάλλος, the Greek family of this verse's καλλονή) and the two need two words. MS1932 *a nós, porção bela de Jacob* explains. *quam* is feminine (the beauty is what he loved), which Portuguese *que* cannot show; *ele* supplies the hidden subject (God).

The Latin says *in voce* twice in the psalm (46:2 *in voce exsultatiónis*, 46:6 *in voce tubæ*), and vox is *voz*. *à voz da trombeta* keeps the word, as 41:8 *à voz das vossas cataratas* keeps it for water; *ao som da trombeta* (DRB 'the sound', MS1932) is the idiom but drops the repetition. *com voz de trombeta* would give the Lord a trumpet's voice. The colon is the response of the Ascension versicle (*R. Et Dóminus in voce tubæ*, Pasc5-4, Benedictio mensae) and reads alone.

options.label: com voz de trombeta
options.note: = 46:2's preposition; heard as the Lord's voice being a trumpet's.

decisions.latin: Psállite Deo nostro, psállite: * psállite Regi nostro, psállite.
decisions.why: psállere → *entoar salmos* (D25), which named this verse as the place its two words would weigh most. The Latin says the same word four times; D2 keeps repetitions, so it is *entoai salmos* four times, +4 syllables a colon, and each colon ends on the paroxytone *salmos*. MS1932 drops the noun in the repeats (*Cantai salmos ao nosso Deus, cantai*) — the verb is still repeated, but the bare *entoai* ends the colon on an oxytone and is not how the row's verb is said elsewhere. The Epiphany antiphon (horas Sancti/01-06) joins this verse to 46:8b (*… psállite sapiénter*), so it must also read with the next verse's second colon.

options.label: entoai salmos … entoai
options.note: MS1932's shape (*Cantai salmos … cantai*); lighter, oxytone colon-ends.

decisions.why: sapiénter, 'wisely' (συνετῶς, 'with understanding'); DRB 'sing ye wisely', MS1932 *sàbiamente*. One adverb for one; *com sabedoria* is the noun of 18:8 and 36:30 (sapiéntia), and a syllable longer. DM1962 *com toda a vossa arte* is the Hebrew's *maskil*, not the Latin.

decisions.latin: Deus sedet super sedem sanctam suam
decisions.why: sedet is a present of state (κάθηται): God sits enthroned. *está sentado* (MS1932) says the state; *se senta* is heard as the act of sitting down. 28:10 *sedébit Dóminus Rex* → *se sentará* is a future, where the act is right. sedes (God's) → *trono* (row), sanctus → adjective after (as *monte santo*). The Latin's future *Regnábit* (against the Greek aorist ἐβασίλευσεν) is kept: *reinará* (rule 1).

options.label: se senta
options.note: 28:10's verb in the present; the act, not the state.

decisions.why: congregári of people gathering (συνήχθησαν). 2:2 has the same Greek verb with the same subject (*príncipes convenérunt* → *os príncipes se reuniram*), so *se reuniram* makes the princes' gathering sound alike in both psalms (MS1932 *reuniram-se*). 34:15 needed *juntaram-se* for *congregáta sunt* only because *convenérunt* (*se reuniram*) stands in the same verse; here nothing competes. *congregaram-se* is the cognate, and 15:4b *congregarei* uses it actively. No glossary row yet; proposed open.

The Greek reads τοῦ θεοῦ οἱ κραταιοὶ τῆς γῆς, 'the mighty ones of the earth are God's'; the Gallican Latin has *dii*, 'the strong gods of the earth' (DRB, MS1932 *os deuses fortes da terra*). The Latin is followed (rule 1). It leaves open whether the *dii* are gods or mighty men called gods (as 81:6 *Ego dixi: Dii estis*), and the Portuguese keeps both. The palm procession (missa Quad6-0r) quotes the verse with *Dei fortes* — the Greek's reading — not the psalter's. fortes → *fortes* (row).

eleváti sunt (ἐπήρθησαν). The eleváre row gives *elevar-se* for a passive with middle sense (8:2b *se elevou*); here the Latin leaves open whether the mighty were raised (by God) or raised themselves, and *se elevaram* leans to the second. The passive keeps it open. veheménter → *muito* (row; 20:2 *exultará muito*). MS1932 *foram extraordinàriamente exaltados*; exaltáre is another verb (row *exaltar*), so *elevados* stays.

options.label: se elevaram muito
options.note: the eleváre row's middle form; leans to self-exaltation.

options.label: foram grandemente elevados
options.note: the valde row's option for weight at a cadence.

choices.46:2: gentes → *nações* (row); *Omnes gentes* as vocative → *Todas as nações* (9:18, 117:10 *todas as nações*). *in voce exsultatiónis* → *com voz de exultação*, word for word 41:5b. The whole verse is the Introit of Pentecost VII (Pent07-0) and the Alleluia verse of the Ascension Mass (missa Pasc5-4) — grep; each colon reads alone.
choices.46:3: excélsus → *excelso*, the Latin's adjective, kept apart from *Altíssimo* (Altíssimus) though the Greek has ὕψιστος. *Rex magnus* → *grande Rei*, without article, in apposition as the Latin; Rei capitalized for God (5:3, 23:7). *super omnem terram* → *sobre toda a terra*. First colon −3 syllables against the Latin (the asyndeton kept); accepted.
choices.46:5: *Elégit nobis* → *Escolheu para nós* (eligere → *escolher*, 32:12, 24:12). *hereditátem suam* is 'his inheritance' in the Latin and Greek (the Hebrew has 'our'); kept. dilígere → *amar* (row).
choices.46:6: ascéndere → *subir* (17:9, 17:11, 23:3); the Latin's verb-first order kept, as natural in Portuguese. The Ascension's versicle and antiphon (Pasc5-4 etc.) quote the verse with *in jubilatióne*, not the psalm's *in júbilo*; the psalm keeps its own words, and the same Portuguese would serve both (see `jubilate`). The two colons are said as V and R: each reads alone.
choices.46:7: Four times *entoai salmos*: +4 syllables in each colon, accepted under D25 and D2 (see `psallite`). *Deo nostro*, *Regi nostro* → *ao nosso Deus*, *ao nosso Rei* (article before possessive).
choices.46:8: *Rex omnis terræ Deus* has God as subject (ὁ θεός with the article; DRB, MS1932): *Deus é o Rei de toda a terra*, natural order (D2). The Palm Sunday procession (missa Quad6-0r) sets this verse as a versicle.
choices.46:9: *Regnábit* future (the Greek aorist not followed). *Deus … Deus* kept at the head of each colon.
choices.46:10: *cum Deo Ábraham* → *com o Deus de Abraão* (μετὰ τοῦ θεοῦ Αβρααμ); DM1962's *ao povo do Deus de Abraão* is the Hebrew. *quóniam* → *porque*.

audit.note: Latin = DO Psalm46.txt, 9 prayed verses (46:2–46:10; no titulus, D7). One mediant per verse, no flex. Uses by grep (ps032/uses.py): 46:2 Introit of Pentecost VII (missa Pent07-0) and Alleluia verse of the Ascension (missa Pasc5-4); the whole psalm in the palm procession (missa Quad6-0r, with *Dei fortes* in 46:10 and *sedit* in 46:9); 46:6 in another Latin (*in jubilatióne*) as the Ascension's versicle, responsory, antiphon, Offertory and Alleluia (horas/missa Pasc5-4, Pasc6-0, Sancti/10-07, Benedictio mensae); 46:7 + 8b as the Epiphany antiphon (horas Sancti/01-06).

Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps046.md (Latin, LXX, WLC, DRB, MS1932, DM1962); DO's Portuguese not used (D12). Rulings applied: D25 (psállere, fourfold in 46:7), D23 not met, glossary rows gentes/pópuli, subjícere (8:8), sub, sedes → trono, dilígere, fortes, valde/veheménter, eleváre, 41:5b *com voz de exultação*. Latin kept against the Greek/Hebrew: 46:9 future *reinará*, 46:10 *deuses fortes* (Greek 'God's mighty ones'), 46:5 *a sua herança*. New proposals: jubiláre family → *aclamar / aclamação* (frees *júbilo* for the gáudium row), terríbilis → *terrível*, spécies (καλλονή) → *beleza*, congregári (people) → *reunir-se*.

Draft 1: hard pass. Length: 46:7 both colons +5 (D25's two words, four times) and the in-verse rhyme *salmos/salmos* — the Latin's own repetition (*psállite … psállite*), accepted; 46:2b −3 (41:5b's formula *com voz de exultação*), 46:5b +3 (*ele* supplied), 46:8b +3 (*entoai salmos* for *psállite*), accepted. Oxytone cadences where the Latin is paroxytone (46:2b *exultação*, 46:4 *nós*, *pés*, 46:5b *amou*, 46:6a *aclamações*, 46:9a *nações*, 46:10a *Abraão*): rule 4 allows the last syllable.
